title: Alternating Arcs on a Color Ring
statement:
Tiles are arranged in a circle. colors[i] is 0 or 1, and the last tile is next to the first one.

An alternating arc is a run of exactly k consecutive tiles around the circle in which every two neighbouring tiles inside the run have different colours.

Return how many starting positions i (from 0 to n − 1) begin an alternating arc. An arc may wrap past the end of the array back to the start.

examples.why: Arcs starting at 0, 1 and 2 alternate. Starting at 3 gives 1, 0, 0 and at 4 gives 0, 0, 1: the wrap joins two 0 tiles.
With k = n every start gives a full lap, and an even ring that alternates works from all 4 starts.
Only the arcs starting at 1 (0, 1, 0) and 2 (1, 0, 1) alternate.

hints: An arc of k tiles alternates exactly when all of its k − 1 inner neighbour pairs differ.
Walk around the circle and keep the length of the current alternating run. Each time the run is at least k long, one more arc ends at this tile.
To handle wrap-around, walk n + k − 1 positions using index i mod n, and only count arcs that end at position k − 1 or later in the walk.

explain.intuition:
Checking each start separately costs O(k) per start. Instead, count arcs by where they end. Walk the tiles in order and keep run, the length of the alternating stretch that ends at the current tile: it grows by one when this tile differs from the previous one, and resets to 1 otherwise. If run ≥ k, the last k tiles alternate, so exactly one arc ends here.

The circle is handled by walking a little past the end: n + k − 1 steps with index i mod n. Arcs that end at walk positions k − 1 through n + k − 2 correspond one-to-one to the n starting positions, so each start is counted once.
steps: For j from 1 to n + k − 2: if colors[j mod n] ≠ colors[(j − 1) mod n], increase run; otherwise set run = 1.
If j ≥ k − 1 and run ≥ k, add one to count.
pitfalls: Ignoring the wrap. In the first example the arcs starting at 3 and 4 cross the end and both fail there.
Walking 2n positions and counting every arc. With an alternating even ring that counts some starts twice.

solutions.title: Check every start
solutions.idea: For each start, walk k − 1 neighbour pairs around the circle and stop at the first equal pair.

solutions.title: Running alternation length
solutions.idea: Walk n + k − 1 tiles around the ring, tracking how long the alternating run ending here is. Every position where the run reaches k ends exactly one arc.

followups: Answer many queries with different k on the same ring. What would you precompute?
Tiles can now change colour between queries. Which structure keeps the answer up to date?
